# Creating and resolving share links

> Logged-in users create short affiliate links, list them, and anyone can follow a short link, which redirects (302) to a marketplace page and records the click.

_Part of [domain/marketing](../../units/domain/marketing.md)_

Everything lives in the `marketing` domain, wired by [`ShareLinksModule`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/share-links.module.ts#L15). [`ShareLinksController`](link-click-analytics.md) has four routes: `POST /links` creates a link, `GET /links` lists your own, `GET /links/:code/stats` shows click stats (see [Link click attribution and stats](link-click-analytics.md)), and `GET /l/:code` is the public redirect. The first three need a logged-in user. The redirect allows anonymous callers. When you create a link, `ShareLinkService.create` first checks the destination. Only `http(s)` URLs on the marketplace front-end host (or its `www.` twin) pass, so the shortener can't be used as an open redirect. It also strips any `ref` parameter from the URL. Then it makes the code. If you gave no alias, it takes the next number from [Hand out ids in blocks of 1,000 from Redis](id-lease.md), scrambles it with [Turn sequential ids into random-looking codes](feistel-code-scrambler.md), and writes it in base62. If you gave an alias, it uses that. The link is saved in DynamoDB with a rule that the code must not exist yet, so a taken alias returns 409. The code is then added to a Bloom filter and any cached "not found" for it is dropped. When someone opens `/l/:code`, `resolve` checks the code format, then the Bloom filter (a quick way to say "this code was never created", which gives 404 with no lookup). After that it reads through a cache into DynamoDB and ignores expired links. The controller adds `ref=<code>` to the destination so attribution follows the user to checkout. It then answers 302 with `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=10`. The click is sent to Kafka without waiting, unless the edge already recorded it. See Record a click without slowing the redirect.

**Look at:** [`ShareLinksController` in share-links.controller.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/api/share-links.controller.ts#L17) · [`ShareLinkService` in share-link.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/share-link.service.ts#L47) · [`scramble` in codes.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/domain/codes.ts#L34) · [`IdLease` in id-lease.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/infra/id-lease.ts#L9) · [`ShareLinksModule` in share-links.module.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/share-links.module.ts#L15)

## Pieces

- [Check that a destination is a marketplace page](destination-validation.md): `validateDestination` rejects non-http(s) URLs and any host other than the front-end host or its `www.` version, and removes `ref` from the URL.
- [Hand out ids in blocks of 1,000 from Redis](id-lease.md): [`IdLease`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/infra/id-lease.ts#L9) takes a block of ids with one Redis `INCRBY` and serves them from memory, so there's one Redis call per 1,000 links.
- [Turn sequential ids into random-looking codes](feistel-code-scrambler.md): [`scramble`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/domain/codes.ts#L39) runs a keyed 4-round Feistel network over 40 bits, so ids map one-to-one to codes that can't be guessed in order, and [`toBase62`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/domain/codes.ts#L9) writes them as 7 characters.
- [Look up a code through Bloom filter, cache and DynamoDB](resolve-pipeline.md): `resolve` checks the code format, then the Bloom filter, then a cache with negative caching, then DynamoDB, and drops expired links.
- Record a click without slowing the redirect: `recordClick` builds a `link.clicked` event with a new click id and sends it to Kafka in the background, unless the `x-edge-click-recorded` header says the edge already did.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `DynamoDB table `Links` (index ``byOwner``)` | Holds one item per link, keyed by `code`. Creation writes it with a not-exists condition. Resolve reads it. `mine` queries the `byOwner` index for the newest 100. |
| cache | ``link:v1:<code>`` | Caches resolved links (1 hour, stale up to a day) and missing codes (60 seconds). |
| cache | ``share-links:id-seq` and `share-links:bloom` in Redis` | The id counter used for leasing blocks of ids, and the Bloom filter of created codes. |
| event | ```link.clicked`` (Kafka, domain `links`)` | Sent on each redirect, keyed by code, carrying click id, time, country and referer. |
| database | `ClickHouse ``link_clicks_minute``` | `stats` reads clicks per minute for the last 7 days. |
| api | ``GET /l/:code`, `POST /links`, `GET /links`` | The public redirect, the create route (rate-limited as `discussion.write`) and the owner's list. |

## Also relies on

- [Link click attribution and stats](link-click-analytics.md): Click events and the stats endpoint rely on it to store and show clicks.

## Watch out

- Codes are Feistel-scrambled ids, so they never collide and no retry loop exists. Only custom aliases can clash, and those return 409.
- The 302 is cached publicly for 10 seconds, so a viral link may be served by the CDN without hitting the origin.
- The Bloom filter check treats a Redis failure as "might exist", so it fails open to the cache and DynamoDB.
- Stats go through `resolve` and check `ownerId`, so another user's code returns 404, not 403.
